thread:
PD-Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert INC-2026-5472 — GPU pool exhaustion in us-east1-primary. Autoscaler failing to add replicas (errors: quota_exceeded / launch_timeout). Pushing page to infra-oncall. https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-5472
Marta: acked. I’m on call. what’s the user impact? any customers paged?
Samir: quick telemetry:
- queue length for us-east1-primary inference queue jumped from ~200 to 14k in 6m
- 5xx spikes: 503 gateway (throttled) for ~12m, tail latency > 10s for many requests
- autoscaler logs: repeated "failed to create instance: quota_exceeded" and occasional "launch_timeout" when trying to attach GPUs
- spillover started triggering but routing policy limited to same-region pools so most requests queued
Lex: looking at the routing config — policy is set to prefer primary region until queue > X, but max_spillover_per_minute = 50 and target pool sizes in eu-west1 are smaller. We need to allow broader cross-region spillover + temporary model variant fallback.
Ira: on it. Can we temporarily relax routing to send non-SLA traffic to eu-west1 and ap-south1? need a quick guardrail: only for non-enterprise/tiered customers and only for model v1 variants.
Hua: preparing manual interventions:
- will attempt a manual scale up of the dedicated reserved pool (us-east1-dedicated-gpu) to add 6 nodes (if quota allows)
- will also flip routing allow_spillover=true for non-prod and standard tiers
- command I'll run:
```bash
# add replicas to gpu pool
redwood infra scale --region us-east1 --pool reserved-gpu --replicas 6 --reason "INC-2026-5472 temporary scale-up"
```
Marta: Samir — can you surface top impacted customers and whether any are on enterprise plans? we need to prioritize support/CS outreach.
Samir: pulling list now. preliminary: ~37 customer keys hit elevated error rates, of which 5 are enterprise (they have dedicated pools but some are routed through shared fallback). Impact: ~12% global request drop for text-gen endpoints routed to us-east1.
Diego: I'll draft a short CS blurb for affected customers and coordinate 1:1 pings for the five enterprise accounts.
Lex: to reduce pressure on queues, propose enabling degraded-mode auto-fallback to quantized variants for standard customers (gpt-large->gpt-large-8bit). This will reduce GPU memory / allow more concurrent sessions while preserving outputs for most users. Also throttle token_budget per-minute for heavy keys.
Ira: agree. We need two things now: (1) enable cross-region spillover for standard tier and (2) flip degrade_to_quantized for standard tier. I'll run the following patch in config service:
```json
{"routing": {"allow_cross_region_spillover": true, "spillover_tiers": ["standard", "dev"]}, "fallbacks": {"degrade_to_quantized": ["standard"]}}
```
Hua: tried manual scale — cloud API returned quota_exceeded on GPU quota for us-east1 (we hit provider limit). I opened support-req with cloud provider (ticket CP-98421) requesting emergency quota raise. ETA unknown.
Marta: since manual scale blocked, prioritize routing + fallback. Lex, Ira — do you have a safe rollout plan? risk of model mismatch?
Lex: rollout steps:
1) route 20% of standard-tier traffic to eu-west1 and ap-south1 (round-robin) with a short TTL for route decisions
2) simultaneously enable degrade_to_quantized for the same 20% cohort
3) monitor token-cost, latency, and error-rate for 5 minutes, then increase to 50% if stable
We can exclude enterprise keys via an allowlist.
Samir: starting metric watch: adding dashboards: queue_length_us-east1, requests_503, cross_region_rtt. Setting alert if eu-west1 latency > 2x baseline.
Diego: sending CS note to enterprise A, B, C with interim mitigation and expected next update in 30m.
Oncall-Bot: Action items tracked: (1) open cloud quota ticket CP-98421 (Hua) (2) enable cross-region spillover for standard tiers (Ira) (3) enable quantized fallback for standard tiers (Lex) (4) CS notifications (Diego) (5) monitor & rollback plan (Samir). Assigning tasks and starting incident timeline.
Hua: spillover toggled. Running traffic split:
```bash
redwood route update --service inference --split "us-east1:80,eu-west1:10,ap-south1:10" --filters "tier:standard,exclude:enterprise" --reason "INC-2026-5472 emergency spillover"
```
Samir: seeing immediate drop in us-east1 queue from 14k -> 4.2k within 90s. eu-west1 rps +12%, ap-south1 +8%. 503s decreasing. tail latency improving for split cohort.
Marta: great. any customer complaints so far? Diego?
Diego: CS pings sent, two enterprise customers requested SLA guarantees — we routed their keys to dedicated fallback pools manually and opened support bridges. The rest are seeing degraded quantized responses, acceptable per their traffic patterns.
Lex: after monitoring for 10m, metrics stable. recommend expanding split to us-east1:50, eu-west1:25, ap-south1:25 for standard tiers to reduce us-east1 pressure further. Also suggest lowering per-key RPS for the heaviest 20 keys by 30% temporarily.
Ira: implementing config bump now. also adding a fast circuit-breaker: when queue_length > 5k AND 503_rate > 1% for a region, automatically increase cross-region spillover by +20%.
Hua: cloud provider responded to ticket — they can increase quota but need manual approval and ~45m lead time. Meanwhile I've confirmed additional GPU capacity in our eu-west1 partner pool for emergency bursts.
Samir: alerting: overall error budget impact capped at ~0.9% for the last 20m, but user-visible 503s peaked at 12 minutes earlier. Historical SLOs for standard tier at 99.0% — we'll breach if this persists > 35m.
Marta: summarizing current state: (1) primary cause: sudden GPU pool exhaustion + autoscaler blocked by cloud quota; (2) immediate mitigations: manual scale blocked, we enabled cross-region spillover + degraded quantized fallback for standard tier, throttled top keys, routed enterprise keys to dedicated fallback pools; (3) impact: partial degradation for standard customers, no major enterprise outages thanks to manual routing; (4) next: wait for cloud quota increase, prepare postmortem.
Lex: recommend follow-ups for postmortem: - autoscaler should be more aware of cloud quota errors and fallback to spillover earlier - routing policy thresholds too conservative for sudden surges - consider reserved emergency pool in secondary regions for failover - improve per-customer backpressure controls
Diego: I've logged customer tickets and compiled list of customers to follow up. CS will send a detailed incident notice tomorrow with mitigations and timeline.
Oncall-Bot: Handoff: Marta -> Diego for follow-up and next-shift oncall. Incident status: mitigated, monitoring. Please ack to accept handoff.
Marta: handing off now, Diego please take ownership for post-incident actions and external comms.
Diego: acked. I'll own the postmortem and CS comms.
Samir: final metrics snapshot before handoff: us-east1 queue 1.1k, total 503s trending to baseline, cross-region rps stabilized.
Hua: cloud quota approved — provisioning scheduled in ~40m, will scale up us-east1 after capacity available to reduce spillover.
Marta: closing incident channel for active paging. We'll create postmortem doc and link here. Great work everyone. :white_check_mark:
PD-Bot: Incident INC-2026-5472 status updated to: mitigated. Postmortem required. Reference: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-5472/postmortem
Oncall-Bot: Reminder: runbook tasks to complete: add autoscaler handling for quota_exceeded, update routing thresholds, schedule reserved emergency pool in eu-west1. Assigned to: Lex, Ira, Product infra. Due: 3 business days.
